pending_commit.commit_message: Revert "CHROMIUM: Revert "mm: remove optimizations based on i_size in mapping writeback waits"" This reverts commit b96b564105d53e4318b34715577a6ba44aef901b. The above mentioned commit was a temporary fix which optimized calls to filemap_fdatawait_keep_errors() so that the range being waited upon was limited to the current size of the inode. This prevented excessive waits as described here: https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-block/msg38204.html and in the bugs in the BUG line below. However, we now have a real fix which is destined for upstream: https://patchwork.kernel.org/cover/11007125/ so use that instead. FROMLIST: jbd2: introduce jbd2_inode dirty range scoping Currently both journal_submit_inode_data_buffers() and journal_finish_inode_data_buffers() operate on the entire address space of each of the inodes associated with a given journal entry. The consequence of this is that if we have an inode where we are constantly appending dirty pages we can end up waiting for an indefinite amount of time in journal_finish_inode_data_buffers() while we wait for all the pages under writeback to be written out. The easiest way to cause this type of workload is do just dd from /dev/zero to a file until it fills the entire filesystem. This can cause journal_finish_inode_data_buffers() to wait for the duration of the entire dd operation. We can improve this situation by scoping each of the inode dirty ranges associated with a given transaction. We do this via the jbd2_inode structure so that the scoping is contained within jbd2 and so that it follows the lifetime and locking rules for that structure. This allows us to limit the writeback & wait in journal_submit_inode_data_buffers() and journal_finish_inode_data_buffers() respectively to the dirty range for a given struct jdb2_inode, keeping us from waiting forever if the inode in question is still being appended to. FROMGIT: mmc: sdhci: sdhci-pci-o2micro: Correctly set bus width when tuning The O2Micro controller only supports tuning at 4-bits. So the host driver needs to change the bus width while tuning and then set it back when done. There was a bug in the original implementation in that mmc->ios.bus_width also wasn't updated. Thus setting the incorrect blocksize in sdhci_send_tuning which results in a tuning failure. power: Wait for external display on resuming with lid closed. Currently if the device resumes with lid still closed, we trigger lid closed action again. Also if the idle delay has expired, we trigger idle action too. This change as part of wake on Docked feature intends to wait for external displays for |KResuspendOnClosedLidTimeout|. This gives enough time for chrome to configure external displays if it recognizes one and tell powerd about it. Powerd on receiving a DisplayModeChange D-Bus call from chrome will treat it as user activity. Why wait here and not in SuspendDelayController ? SuspendDelays intend to give all deamons enough time to do stuff before suspend. Thus this should give chrome enough time to do the configuration. But chrome to prevent flicker in dark resume does not configure external displays when in suspend resume path. Thus let us not trigger suspendImminent immediately. Let us give chrome enough time to recognize external displays. BUG=chromium:786721 TEST=Deploy on nocturne and test the use case. Change-Id: I142493db5a73535d5016321c6545794fc10a97f4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1651997 Tested-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@google.com>
